name: Helen Keller
role: American author and activist; Socialist Party and IWW member (1880-1968)
summary: A deafblind author and lecturer who became a committed socialist after studying the industrial causes of blindness, joining the Socialist Party in 1909 and later the IWW, which she thought less tied to electoral politics. She opposed war and militarism as products of capitalist exploitation, backed women's suffrage, unions and the NAACP, defended the Russian Revolution, and in 1915 endorsed birth control and withholding surgery from a severely impaired infant on eugenic grounds.

universal-healthcare.rationale: In 1915 she said the State should govern every department of industry, health and education to keep the people sound in body and mind; she did not speak of healthcare insurance as such.

raise-minimum-wage.rationale: Repeatedly demanded a living wage for all workers and for women; no statutory minimum wage figure is given.

markets-allocate-better.rationale: Described the market as a blind force of necessity that leaves workers unable to buy what they make, and the capitalist system as the chief evil behind unemployment.

public-ownership.rationale: Asked whether railroads should be nationalized and said the State should govern every department of industry; she endorsed collective ownership of essential industries.

unions-good.rationale: Said she was glad of every effort workingmen make to organize and that conditions improve only when they stand together.

property-fundamental.rationale: Endorsed workers taking possession of the resources and machinery of production; saw private ownership of the means of livelihood as the root of injustice.

regulate-corporations.rationale: Called for factory safeguards, clean food, an end to child labour and a living wage to be imposed on employers, and blamed profit-driven neglect of safeguards for blindness.

cut-welfare.rationale: Mixed: she opposed degrading pensions for the blind in favour of paid work, but demanded state action against poverty and said poverty is structural, not the fault of the poor.

worker-ownership.rationale: Endorsed the IWW principle that workers in their collectivity must own and operate all essential industrial institutions and that creators of wealth should own what they create.

state-harmful.rationale: Said the State should govern every department of industry, health and education.

empower-police-military.rationale: Opposed a larger army and navy ("preparedness") and said the army could be used to break strikes.

correct-racial-injustice.rationale: Sent money to the NAACP and condemned lynching and the denial of constitutional rights.

gradual-change.rationale: Said education without revolution is impossible, rejected gradual reform and wanted conditions bettered at once.

nation-first.rationale: Said she looked on the whole world as her fatherland and on true patriotism as the brotherhood of man.

revolution-justified.rationale: Asked "education or revolution?" she answered "Revolution"; later signed a letter "Yours for the revolution".

central-planning.rationale: Wanted the State to govern every department of industry and called the market blind; she did not discuss planning mechanics.

abolish-money-wages.rationale: Quoted and endorsed the IWW aim to abolish the wage system, calling its demands just.

monarchy-legitimate.rationale: Called on workers to junk their masters' kings and customs.

political-violence-never.rationale: Said she was not for peace at all hazards, never regretted the blood of the French Revolution, and sympathised with the oppressed driven to use force.

military-superiority.rationale: Called fear of invasion absurd and opposed building up arms and navy.

class-struggle-history.rationale: Called the IWW a union based on the class struggle and said history shows economic interests are the strongest ties binding men; also wrote that wars arise from exploitation.

limit-population.rationale: Wrote that to preserve the race people must now hold back the power of propagation, through voluntary birth control by families.

direct-action.rationale: Mixed: in 1916 she said nothing can be gained by political action and workers must organize economically; in 1917 she endorsed voting for the Socialist candidate Hillquit.

production-for-use.rationale: Complained that the output of a mill is valued above healthy, free human beings and that safeguards are skipped to protect profit.

profit-exploitation.rationale: Said the owner of a machine takes the profit while the worker gets no share, and that workers are exploited for the benefit of others.

capitalism-causes-war.rationale: Said every modern war has its root in exploitation, that capitalists want armaments because they beget war, and that militarism is a bulwark of capitalism.

conscription.rationale: Said citizens are within their rights to agitate for abolition of conscription and urged workers not to be obedient soldiers.

positive-liberty.rationale: Said the ballot does not make a free man of a wage slave and that she could not be free while others lacked a living wage.

total-state.rationale: She wanted the State to run industry, health and education but also defended free speech and assembly and did not speak of controlling culture.

territorial-expansion.rationale: Opposed US overseas holdings and foreign investments protected by arms ("Drop island possessions").

workplace-democracy.rationale: Endorsed workers collectively owning and operating the essential industries.

national-self-determination.rationale: Demanded enforcement of the proposition that every nation has the right to govern itself.

class-collaboration.rationale: Said there can be no compromise while workers live in want and masters in luxury.

workers-nation.rationale: Called for a militant international union of workers and a world-wide union rather than national organization.

racial-segregation-law.rationale: Wrote in 1951 that she was against all segregation in spirit and principle.

state-class-instrument.rationale: Said the dominant parties are managed by the propertied classes for their profit and that the owners rule because they own the means of life, press, church and school.

patriarchy-structural.rationale: Said men made women's laws, were their judge and jailer, and that man-made laws leave women at their mercy.

heritable-defect-limits.rationale: Contested: in 1915 she wrote that society faces questions of eugenics and birth control and said the world is flooded with persons who should never have been born, but she also asked how any mortal can be trusted to decide; she urged voluntary birth control rather than a state ban.

security-forces-accountable.rationale: Protested that nobody was punished for the lynching of Frank Little and the Bisbee deportations.

night-watchman-state.rationale: Said the State should govern every department of industry, health and education.

equal-moral-worth.rationale: Contested: she demanded equal treatment regardless of race, colour, creed or sex, yet in the 1915 Bollinger case she judged that the life of a severely impaired infant was not worth living.

priority-to-poor.rationale: Said the workers' cause was her cause and demanded decent homes, education and wages for all workers first.

restrict-strikes-picketing.rationale: Supported strikers, condemned the imprisonment of workers for striking, and urged a strike against war.

population-causes-poverty.rationale: Said the miseries of the poor are not mainly their own faults and attributed unemployment and want to the system of production, not numbers.

emergency-suspend-protections.rationale: Protested wartime suppression of free speech, assembly and the press as a betrayal of the Constitution.

material-conditions-drive-history.rationale: Said industry rests on the "iron law of economic determination" and that economic interests are the strongest ties in history.

patriotic-education.rationale: Said schools teach glorification of war and that patriotism of drums and flags serves rulers; she wanted children taught to honour heroes of peace.

capitalism-adapts.rationale: Predicted capitalism would face a starving multitude of unemployed that it could not save itself from.

mass-culture-pacifies.rationale: Said war scares and militarist education distract people from their conditions and that the press conceals news of exploitation; she did not discuss mass culture generally.

ruling-class-consent.rationale: Said the owners hold the press, church and school and that editors obey the money power behind them.

slavery-not-civil-war-cause.rationale: Inferred: she said the Civil War decided whether Southern slaveholders or Northern capitalists would exploit the West, which downplays slavery as its cause; she did not address the question directly.

corporate-influence.rationale: Said the country is governed for the corporations, bankers and exploiters of labour.

non-intervention.rationale: Opposed foreign intervention in Russia and demanded the principle that every nation may govern itself; she did not address every possible reason for intervention.

industrial-unions.rationale: Described and endorsed the IWW principle of industrial unionism and one big union of all industries as opposed to trade unions.

defeat-communism.rationale: Said those who do not stand for fair play to Soviet Russia and for lifting the blockade are friends of Czarism and exploitation.

women-equality-needs-economic-change.rationale: Said women cannot be free apart from the workers and that men's and women's rights are both denied while workers lack ownership and control of their lives.

neither-capitalism-nor-communism.rationale: Rejected capitalism and praised the Soviet republic and Lenin.

suppress-opposition.rationale: Condemned the persecution of the IWW, the denial of assembly and press censorship in 1917-18.

colonies-serve-metropole.rationale: Condemned the plunder of one people by another and wars to decide who shall exploit colonies and weaker countries.

intersecting-oppressions.rationale: Tied women's subjection to wage exploitation and called for solidarity regardless of race, colour, creed or sex.

alienated-labor.rationale: Described workers herded among machines whose product is not theirs until they are hardened and brutalized.

press-owned-by-wealth.rationale: Said the leading newspapers conceal the truth about workers and that the money power behind the press opposes Socialism.

racial-franchise.rationale: Condemned the denial of constitutional rights to citizens of colour and urged solidarity regardless of race, colour, creed or sex; she did not address a racial franchise by name.

wealth-concentration-endangers-liberty.rationale: Said that when a few own the means of livelihood the many are not free and democracy is a name.

charity-over-state-aid.rationale: Called charity superficial and said Socialism goes to the root of poverty and charity.

women-in-religious-leadership.rationale: Mocked the "Woman, be silent" ban from the pulpit and the idea that theology is closed to women.

income-for-work-not-ownership.rationale: Wrote that society must move to a state in which every hand works and reaps the fruits of its own endeavour, and mocked hands that produce nothing being exalted.

socialism-needs-workers-power.rationale: Said workers themselves must secure their freedom and grow strong.

family-wage.rationale: Demanded a living wage giving every worker a decent home and standard of living; she did not name family size.

women-distinct-values.rationale: Wrote that women are more social than men and would use the ballot to prevent war.

arms-reduction.rationale: Said money wasted on guns could build clean towns and that the best preparedness disarms other nations' hostility; she did not name a level of reduction.

soldiers-refuse-war.rationale: Urged workers to strike against war and not to be "dumb, obedient slaves in an army of destruction".

workers-own-party.rationale: Joined the Socialist Party, said the old parties serve the ruling class, and in 1917 said she would vote for the Socialist Hillquit; in 1916 she called the party too slow.

women-property-inheritance.rationale: Criticised laws under which women cannot hold property and their wages belong to fathers or husbands.

women-suffrage.rationale: Argued that women need and should have the vote and called women's enfranchisement part of the movement to enfranchise all mankind.

religion-oppresses-women.rationale: Described church teaching and priestcraft as degrading and subjugating women; she remained religious herself.

defend-planned-state.rationale: Condemned the blockade and military intervention against Soviet Russia and called its cause just.

unjust-law-not-binding.rationale: Wrote in 1914 that no one had given her a good reason why unjust laws should be obeyed.

labour-theory-of-value.rationale: Endorsed the claim that creators of wealth are entitled to the full value of their product.

patriotism-serves-workers.rationale: Mixed: she scorned workers' loyalty to a country that exploits them but defined true patriotism as the service of all to all.

notes: Views shifted from Socialist Party membership (1909) to the IWW (about 1912-16, when she said nothing can be gained by political action), yet in 1917 she endorsed voting for the Socialist Hillquit; direction-of-change answers are marked low. Her 1915 Bollinger baby article defended Dr. Haiselden's refusal to operate and endorsed birth control with eugenic reasoning; it is recorded under heritable-defect-limits and equal-moral-worth at low confidence because she also doubted anyone's fitness to judge, and no statement covers infant euthanasia exactly. No evidence found on the death penalty, abortion, or sex education. Not read: Foner, Helen Keller: Her Socialist Years (lending-only on archive.org); disabilitymuseum.org was unreachable (HTTP 406).
